reason: The hypothesis relies on a specific dislocation-mechanism shift (screw-to-edge) to retain high-temperature strength, but the cited evidence only shows this mechanism for MoNbTaVW (E3) and does not demonstrate that W addition to TiVNbTa would induce the same shift. The general high-temperature strength retention of Mo-containing RHEAs (E1, E2) provides only indirect support, and no evidence is cited for W's effect on lattice distortion or dislocation character in TiVNbTa.
premises: W addition dissolves into BCC matrix and increases lattice distortion
Increased lattice distortion promotes a shift from screw- to edge-dominated dislocation slip at high temperature
Edge-dislocation control at high temperature retains yield strength better than screw-dislocation control
Mo-containing RHEAs (e.g., MoNbTaW, MoNbTaVW) show lower reduction in yield strength at elevated temperatures
TiVNbTa baseline has significantly lower strength at 1273 K (~330–423 MPa) than at room temperature (~800 MPa)
